axis: incident disclosure window: confirmed data exfiltration vs contained-intrusion-only incident
rule_template: An organization experiencing <<CATEGORY_A>> incident must notify the relevant regulator within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of discovery, and an organization experiencing <<CATEGORY_B>> incident must notify the relevant regulator within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of discovery.
scenario_template_a: Meridian Health Systems detected unauthorized outbound transfers of patient billing records following a spear-phishing campaign that compromised an administrator's credentials. Forensic analysis confirmed that approximately 40,000 records left the network before the affected server was isolated. The security team documented the exfiltration timeline and notified internal leadership <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compromise was discovered.
scenario_template_b: Castlebrook Financial detected an intrusion attempt on its internal network after log analysis revealed lateral movement by an unauthorized account across three servers. Forensic analysis confirmed that the actor was contained before any data left the network, with no evidence of exfiltration. The security team documented the incident timeline and notified internal leadership <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compromise was discovered.

axis: ransomware incident reporting timeline: ransom paid vs ransom demanded but not paid
rule_template: Organizations that experience <<CATEGORY_A>> incident must report the incident to the sector regulator within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the event, and organizations that experience <<CATEGORY_B>> incident must report the incident to the sector regulator within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the event.
scenario_template_a: Halcyon Manufacturing suffered a ransomware attack that encrypted its production-scheduling servers via credential dumping and lateral movement from an initial phishing email. The company's leadership authorized payment of the ransom to obtain a decryption key. The compliance team reported the incident to the sector regulator <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the encryption was discovered.
scenario_template_b: Brightpoint Logistics suffered a ransomware attack that encrypted several file servers via credential dumping and lateral movement from an initial phishing email. The company's leadership declined to pay the ransom and instead restored systems from offline backups. The compliance team reported the incident to the sector regulator <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the encryption was discovered.

axis: individual-notification record-count threshold: consumer-data breach vs employee-data breach
rule_template: An organization that suffers <<CATEGORY_A>> breach affecting more than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> must directly notify each affected individual, and an organization that suffers <<CATEGORY_B>> breach affecting more than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> must directly notify each affected individual.
scenario_template_a: Vantage Retail discovered that an attacker used SQL injection against its e-commerce platform to access a database containing customer names, emails, and payment tokens. Log review determined that the exposed database contained data belonging to <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> of customers. The incident response team is finalizing its notification list this week.
scenario_template_b: Vantage Retail's HR division discovered that an attacker used SQL injection against an internal payroll application to access a database containing staff names, emails, and salary details. Log review determined that the exposed database contained data belonging to <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> of employees. The incident response team is finalizing its notification list this week.

axis: critical vulnerability remediation deadline: internet-facing system vs internal-only system
rule_template: Agencies must remediate critical vulnerabilities on <<CATEGORY_A>> system within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of identification, and agencies must remediate critical vulnerabilities on <<CATEGORY_B>> system within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of identification.
scenario_template_a: Coreline Utilities' vulnerability scanning tool flagged a critical remote-code-execution flaw in a customer-facing web portal reachable from the public internet. The vulnerability management team logged the finding and scheduled remediation work. The patch was ultimately deployed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the finding was logged.
scenario_template_b: Coreline Utilities' vulnerability scanning tool flagged a critical remote-code-execution flaw in an internal scheduling application accessible only from the corporate network. The vulnerability management team logged the finding and scheduled remediation work. The patch was ultimately deployed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the finding was logged.

axis: log retention exemption scope: security-incident-related logs vs routine-operational logs
rule_template: Organizations must retain <<CATEGORY_A>> logs for at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> after collection, and organizations must retain <<CATEGORY_B>> logs for at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> after collection.
scenario_template_a: After containing an intrusion attributed to a known ransomware affiliate, Palmetto Bank's security operations center preserved the authentication and network-flow logs tied directly to the incident for review by outside forensic investigators. Those specific logs were retained on the SOC's archival storage for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before the retention policy was reassessed.
scenario_template_b: As part of its standard IT operations, Palmetto Bank's security operations center retains routine server and application logs unrelated to any specific security incident for general auditing purposes. Those routine logs were retained on the SOC's archival storage for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before the retention policy was reassessed.

axis: de minimis incident reporting exemption: malware contained to a single endpoint vs malware spread across multiple endpoints
rule_template: Incidents classified as <<CATEGORY_A>> affecting fewer than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> are exempt from mandatory incident reporting, and incidents classified as <<CATEGORY_B>> affecting fewer than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> are exempt from mandatory incident reporting.
scenario_template_a: Ashgrove Dental Group's IT contractor identified a strain of commodity malware, delivered via a malicious email attachment, that had been contained to isolated workstations before it could spread further across the practice's network. The remediation report logged that the malware had been detected and removed from <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Ashgrove Dental Group's IT contractor identified a strain of commodity malware, delivered via a malicious email attachment, that used lateral movement techniques to spread across multiple workstations and a file server before containment. The remediation report logged that the malware had been detected and removed from <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: third-party risk assessment exemption scope: privileged vendor system access vs reporting-only vendor access
rule_template: Third-party vendors with <<CATEGORY_A>> access lasting more than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> must undergo a full third-party risk assessment, and third-party vendors with <<CATEGORY_B>> access lasting more than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> must undergo a full third-party risk assessment.
scenario_template_a: Quillfield Insurance granted a claims-processing contractor privileged administrative access to its policy management database in order to perform a system migration. The vendor management office logged the access grant and tracked its duration for internal review. The privileged access remained active for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before being revoked.
scenario_template_b: Quillfield Insurance granted an analytics contractor reporting-only, read-access credentials to a summary dashboard in order to generate quarterly usage statistics. The vendor management office logged the access grant and tracked its duration for internal review. The reporting-only access remained active for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before being revoked.

axis: forensic imaging exemption from extended chain-of-custody hold: financial-data system vs marketing-data system
rule_template: Following a suspected compromise, <<CATEGORY_A>> must be forensically imaged within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> to be exempt from the extended chain-of-custody hold, and <<CATEGORY_B>> must be forensically imaged within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> to be exempt from the extended chain-of-custody hold.
scenario_template_a: Ironvale Credit Union identified suspicious authentication attempts on a server hosting core banking transaction records shortly after a phishing campaign targeted several employees. The incident response team scheduled forensic imaging of the affected server as part of the standard response workflow. Imaging of the financial-data server was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the suspicious activity was flagged.
scenario_template_b: Ironvale Credit Union identified suspicious authentication attempts on a server hosting the marketing team's email-campaign content shortly after a phishing campaign targeted several employees. The incident response team scheduled forensic imaging of the affected server as part of the standard response workflow. Imaging of the marketing-data server was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the suspicious activity was flagged.

axis: monitoring data retention limit based on consent basis: explicit-consent monitoring vs implied-consent (banner-notice-only) monitoring
rule_template: Data collected under an <<CATEGORY_A>> monitoring authorization may be retained for up to <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and data collected under an <<CATEGORY_B>> monitoring authorization may be retained for up to <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Dunmore Aerospace requires employees to sign an explicit written consent form acknowledging endpoint monitoring before receiving network credentials, and the security team relies on that signed authorization as the basis for its insider-threat detection program. Packet-capture data collected under this program was retained on the SOC's storage array for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> following collection.
scenario_template_b: Cindergate Media relies solely on a login-banner notice displayed each time an employee accesses the network, without any signed acknowledgment, as the basis for its insider-threat detection program. Packet-capture data collected under this program was retained on the SOC's storage array for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> following collection.

axis: privileged-session recording review window: court-order-authorized monitoring vs internal-policy-authorized monitoring
rule_template: Session recordings gathered under <<CATEGORY_A>> monitoring must be reviewed by the security team within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of collection, and session recordings gathered under <<CATEGORY_B>> monitoring must be reviewed by the security team within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of collection.
scenario_template_a: Following a subpoena and court order authorizing enhanced surveillance of a specific administrator account suspected of data theft, Blackfern Logistics' security team began recording all privileged sessions associated with that account. Recordings gathered under the court order were reviewed by the security team <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after collection.
scenario_template_b: Relying only on its standing internal acceptable-use policy, without any court order, Larkhollow Retail's security team began recording privileged sessions associated with an administrator account flagged by an anomaly-detection alert. Recordings gathered under this internal-policy authorization were reviewed by the security team <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after collection.

axis: keystroke-logging data purge deadline: individualized signed consent vs blanket employment-contract clause
rule_template: Keystroke-logging deployed under <<CATEGORY_A>> authorization must have its collected data purged within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> absent an active investigation, and keystroke-logging deployed under <<CATEGORY_B>> authorization must have its collected data purged within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> absent an active investigation.
scenario_template_a: After a contractor at Fennimore Robotics signed an individualized consent form specific to a fraud investigation, the security team deployed keystroke-logging software on the contractor's workstation with that signed authorization as its basis. In the absence of an active investigation, the collected keystroke data remained stored on the monitoring server for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before deletion.
scenario_template_b: Relying on a blanket monitoring clause embedded in its standard employment contract, Gallowridge Manufacturing's security team deployed keystroke-logging software on an employee's workstation as part of a routine productivity review. In the absence of an active investigation, the collected keystroke data remained stored on the monitoring server for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> before deletion.

axis: breach notification deadline: domestic-only personal data vs cross-border personal data
rule_template: An organization must notify its lead regulator of a breach involving <<CATEGORY_A>> personal data within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of discovery, and an organization must notify its lead regulator of a breach involving <<CATEGORY_B>> personal data within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of discovery.
scenario_template_a: Thistledown Payments discovered that an attacker exploited a misconfigured API to access a database containing payment records exclusively of customers residing within the country where the company is headquartered. Forensic review confirmed no records belonging to residents of other countries were affected. The compliance office finalized its regulator notification <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the breach was discovered.
scenario_template_b: Thistledown Payments discovered that an attacker exploited a misconfigured API to access a database containing payment records of customers residing in several countries across three continents, in addition to domestic customers. Forensic review confirmed that records belonging to residents of multiple foreign jurisdictions were affected. The compliance office finalized its regulator notification <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the breach was discovered.

axis: post-incident data-transfer risk review deadline: domestically stored data vs cross-border-transferred data
rule_template: Following an incident, an organization must complete a data-transfer risk review for <<CATEGORY_A>> data within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and an organization must complete a data-transfer risk review for <<CATEGORY_B>> data within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Oakmere Analytics discovered that a misconfigured storage bucket had briefly exposed a dataset that is stored and processed entirely within its home country, with no replication to any foreign data center. The privacy team initiated the required post-incident review process. The data-transfer risk review for the domestically stored dataset was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the exposure was discovered.
scenario_template_b: Oakmere Analytics discovered that a misconfigured storage bucket had briefly exposed a dataset that is routinely replicated to data centers in two foreign countries as part of the company's global processing arrangement. The privacy team initiated the required post-incident review process. The data-transfer risk review for the cross-border dataset was completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the exposure was discovered.

axis: regulator-notification completion deadline: single-jurisdiction incident vs multi-jurisdiction incident
rule_template: An organization handling a <<CATEGORY_A>> incident must complete all required regulator notifications within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of confirmation, and an organization handling a <<CATEGORY_B>> incident must complete all required regulator notifications within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of confirmation.
scenario_template_a: Redshale Telecom confirmed that a credential-stuffing attack had compromised subscriber accounts belonging solely to customers within its single home jurisdiction, with no subscribers registered in other countries affected. The legal team tracked the notification process to the single relevant regulator. All required regulator notifications were completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compromise was confirmed.
scenario_template_b: Redshale Telecom confirmed that a credential-stuffing attack had compromised subscriber accounts belonging to customers across several countries in which it operates subsidiaries, triggering notification duties to multiple national regulators. The legal team tracked the notification process to each relevant regulator. All required regulator notifications were completed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the compromise was confirmed.

axis: forensic evidence-package retention: shared with domestic law enforcement vs shared with foreign law enforcement
rule_template: Evidence packages that are <<CATEGORY_A>> must be retained for at least <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> to support any resulting proceedings, and evidence packages that are <<CATEGORY_B>> must be retained for at least <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> to support any resulting proceedings.
scenario_template_a: After identifying the intrusion vector used against its network, Copperfield Bank compiled a forensic evidence package and shared it exclusively with its domestic law enforcement agency, since the attacker's infrastructure was traced entirely within the same country. The evidence package was retained in the bank's secure archive for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> to support the ensuing investigation.
scenario_template_b: After identifying the intrusion vector used against its network, Copperfield Bank compiled a forensic evidence package and shared it with a foreign law enforcement partner agency, since the attacker's command-and-control infrastructure was traced to servers located overseas. The evidence package was retained in the bank's secure archive for <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> to support the ensuing investigation.

axis: sector CERT reporting deadline: critical-infrastructure operator vs general commercial business
rule_template: A <<CATEGORY_A>> that suffers a significant cyber incident must report it to the national CERT within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of detection, and a <<CATEGORY_B>> that suffers a significant cyber incident must report it to the national CERT within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of detection.
scenario_template_a: Brackwater Water Authority, which operates municipal water-treatment control systems, detected anomalous commands issued to a programmable logic controller consistent with unauthorized remote access. The operations security team confirmed the intrusion and began the incident-reporting workflow. The report to the national CERT was filed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after detection.
scenario_template_b: Willowmere Office Supplies, a general retail business with no critical-infrastructure operations, detected anomalous commands issued to an internal inventory-management server consistent with unauthorized remote access. The IT security team confirmed the intrusion and began the incident-reporting workflow. The report to the national CERT was filed <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after detection.

axis: mandatory incident-response exercise frequency: critical-infrastructure entity vs general-business entity
rule_template: A <<CATEGORY_A>> entity must conduct a full incident-response exercise at least every <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and a <<CATEGORY_B>> entity must conduct a full incident-response exercise at least every <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Ferrowind Energy, which operates regional power-grid substations classified as critical infrastructure, schedules full incident-response tabletop exercises simulating attacker techniques such as lateral movement and command-and-control beaconing. The most recent exercise was conducted, and the gap since the prior exercise was <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Ashford Bookkeeping, a general small business providing accounting services with no critical-infrastructure designation, schedules incident-response tabletop exercises simulating attacker techniques such as phishing and credential theft. The most recent exercise was conducted, and the gap since the prior exercise was <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: independent security-controls audit frequency: critical-infrastructure operator vs general-business operator
rule_template: A <<CATEGORY_A>> must undergo an independent security-controls audit at least every <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and a <<CATEGORY_B>> must undergo an independent security-controls audit at least every <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Granholt Rail, which operates signaling systems for a regional freight-rail network classified as critical infrastructure, engaged an independent auditor to review its industrial-control-system security controls. The interval between this audit and the previous one was <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Pinehurst Marketing, a general business providing advertising services with no critical-infrastructure designation, engaged an independent auditor to review its corporate network security controls. The interval between this audit and the previous one was <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: affected-endpoint threshold triggering sector-regulator escalation: critical-infrastructure entity vs general-business entity
rule_template: A <<CATEGORY_A>> entity must escalate an incident to its sector regulator once more than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> are affected, and a <<CATEGORY_B>> entity must escalate an incident to its sector regulator once more than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> are affected.
scenario_template_a: Stonebridge Gas Distribution, which operates natural-gas pipeline monitoring infrastructure classified as critical, identified malware spreading via lateral movement across its operational technology network. The incident response team tallied the scope of the compromise. A total of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> were confirmed affected before containment.
scenario_template_b: Marlowe Consulting, a general professional-services firm with no critical-infrastructure designation, identified malware spreading via lateral movement across its corporate IT network. The incident response team tallied the scope of the compromise. A total of <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> were confirmed affected before containment.

axis: breach notification record-count threshold: customer-facing data vs internal-systems-only data
rule_template: A breach affecting a system that processes <<CATEGORY_A>> with more than <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> exposed requires notification to the data-protection authority, and a breach affecting a system that processes <<CATEGORY_B>> with more than <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> exposed requires notification to the data-protection authority.
scenario_template_a: Hallowbrook Airlines discovered that an attacker used stolen credentials obtained through spear-phishing to access its customer-facing booking platform, which stores passenger names and travel itineraries. Forensic review determined that the exposed database contained <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> belonging to booking customers.
scenario_template_b: Hallowbrook Airlines discovered that an attacker used stolen credentials obtained through spear-phishing to access an internal maintenance-scheduling system used only by ground crew, which stores no customer information. Forensic review determined that the exposed database contained <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> belonging to internal maintenance logs.

axis: encryption-at-rest remediation deadline: customer-payment data vs internal-analytics-only data
rule_template: Systems storing <<CATEGORY_A>> discovered to lack encryption-at-rest must be remediated within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of discovery, and systems storing <<CATEGORY_B>> discovered to lack encryption-at-rest must be remediated within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of discovery.
scenario_template_a: During a routine configuration audit, Silverlake Commerce discovered that a database storing customer payment-card tokens and transaction history lacked encryption at rest. The engineering team opened a remediation ticket and tracked it to completion. Encryption was enabled on the customer-payment-data system <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the gap was discovered.
scenario_template_b: During a routine configuration audit, Silverlake Commerce discovered that a database used only for internal sales-analytics dashboards, containing no customer records, lacked encryption at rest. The engineering team opened a remediation ticket and tracked it to completion. Encryption was enabled on the internal-analytics system <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the gap was discovered.

axis: access-log anomaly review cadence: customer personal data systems vs internal DevOps tooling
rule_template: Access logs for systems handling <<CATEGORY_A>> must be reviewed for anomalies at least every <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>>, and access logs for systems handling <<CATEGORY_B>> must be reviewed for anomalies at least every <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_a: Emberton Health Plan's security team is responsible for reviewing access logs from the member portal, which handles customers' personal health and billing information, to detect signs of credential misuse or unauthorized queries. The most recent review cycle showed that logs for the member portal were reviewed every <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.
scenario_template_b: Emberton Health Plan's security team is responsible for reviewing access logs from the internal DevOps deployment-pipeline tooling, which contains no customer records, to detect signs of credential misuse or unauthorized queries. The most recent review cycle showed that logs for the deployment tooling were reviewed every <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>>.

axis: grace period for new logging-standard compliance: post-effective-date systems vs legacy pre-effective-date systems
rule_template: <<CATEGORY_A>> systems must be brought into compliance with the new centralized-logging standard within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the standard's effective date, and <<CATEGORY_B>> systems must be brought into compliance with the new centralized-logging standard within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the standard's effective date.
scenario_template_a: Nightingale Software rolled out a new customer-facing application server after the updated centralized-logging standard took effect, building it directly on the new logging framework from initial deployment. The compliance team tracked the system's progress toward full alignment with the standard. Full compliance with the new logging standard was reached <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the standard's effective date.
scenario_template_b: Nightingale Software continued operating a legacy inventory-management server that had been deployed years before the updated centralized-logging standard took effect, running on an older logging framework. The compliance team tracked the system's progress toward full alignment with the standard. Full compliance with the new logging standard was reached <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the standard's effective date.

axis: MFA enforcement deadline: newly onboarded accounts vs legacy preexisting accounts
rule_template: <<CATEGORY_A>> user accounts must have multi-factor authentication enforced within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the mandate's effective date, and <<CATEGORY_B>> user accounts must have multi-factor authentication enforced within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the mandate's effective date.
scenario_template_a: Thackeray Consulting created a batch of newly onboarded employee accounts shortly after the company adopted a company-wide multi-factor authentication mandate in response to rising credential-stuffing attacks in its industry. The IT team tracked the rollout of MFA enrollment across these new accounts. MFA enforcement was completed for the newly onboarded accounts <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the mandate's effective date.
scenario_template_b: Thackeray Consulting identified a batch of legacy employee accounts that had existed since before the company adopted its company-wide multi-factor authentication mandate in response to rising credential-stuffing attacks in its industry. The IT team tracked the rollout of MFA enrollment across these legacy accounts. MFA enforcement was completed for the legacy accounts <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the mandate's effective date.

axis: data-minimization retention compliance deadline: post-regime-collected data vs legacy pre-regime-collected data
rule_template: <<CATEGORY_A>> data must be brought into compliance with the new data-minimization retention limits within <<THRESHOLD_A>> <<UNIT>> of the regime's effective date, and <<CATEGORY_B>> data must be brought into compliance with the new data-minimization retention limits within <<THRESHOLD_B>> <<UNIT>> of the regime's effective date.
scenario_template_a: Marrowfield Insurance began collecting customer claims-history data after the jurisdiction's new data-minimization regime took effect, applying the updated retention rules from the point of collection. The privacy office tracked this dataset's alignment with the new retention limits. Full compliance for this post-regime dataset was achieved <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the regime's effective date.
scenario_template_b: Marrowfield Insurance held a large archive of legacy customer claims-history data that had been collected years before the jurisdiction's new data-minimization regime took effect, under the prior, less restrictive retention rules. The privacy office tracked this dataset's alignment with the new retention limits. Full compliance for this legacy dataset was achieved <<VALUE>> <<UNIT>> after the regime's effective date.
